profile.campus: Chandler, Maricopa County, Arizona (CyrusOne Phoenix-metro campus, PHX1-PHX8)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility materials and an aggregator listing dedicated to this specific building, PHX1 sits at 2305-2335 South Ellis Street, Chandler, AZ 85286, part of CyrusOne's roughly 2,000,000 sq ft, eight-building Chandler campus (PHX1 through PHX8) totaling a publicly stated 169 MW of IT capacity across the whole campus; that campus-wide MW figure is not confirmed as this individual building's own capacity, so it is not asserted here as a single-building number.

Wikipedia's entry on CyrusOne states the company acquired 55.9 acres in Chandler in September 2011 for data center construction, part of its early-2010s national expansion under then-parent Cincinnati Bell before CyrusOne's own 2013 IPO; the company was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and was taken private in a roughly $15 billion deal when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it, closing in March 2022. Chandler's electric and water utility, Salt River Project (SRP), serves this part of the Phoenix metro; Arizona data centers' water-intensive cooling systems have drawn scrutiny from local outlets including the Phoenix New Times given the state's arid climate and ongoing water-supply debates, a regional context relevant to this campus though not a site-specific consumption figure confirmed for this particular building.

Chandler's broader appeal to data center operators, alongside CyrusOne, the same submarket has drawn large campuses from other hyperscale and colocation players, stems from Arizona's relatively low natural-disaster risk profile (limited seismic activity, no hurricane exposure), business-friendly tax treatment for data center equipment under state statute, and proximity to fiber routes linking Phoenix to Los Angeles and other West Coast interconnection points, factors industry trade press has repeatedly cited in explaining the Phoenix metro's growth as a secondary US data center hub behind Northern Virginia and Texas.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Chandler campus spans roughly 2,000,000 square feet across eight buildings (PHX1 through PHX8) and publishes a campus-wide IT capacity of 169 MW. This figure represents the aggregate for all eight buildings; the IT capacity of PHX1 alone is not published. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 169 MW across the full campus translates to an assumption of roughly 4,225 racks, though this serves the operator's full Chandler footprint and customer mix rather than AI exclusively.

The campus holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and TIA-942 certifications, qualifying it for regulated workloads including financial services, healthcare, and federal compliance. The Green Globes certification indicates environmental management standards. None of these certifications identify AI tenants specifically.

This campus represents the largest published capacity in Arizona by MW, holding 33% of the state's 512 MW of published data center IT capacity across 56 mapped facilities statewide. Arizona's appeal stems from low natural-disaster risk, favorable tax treatment for data center equipment, and fiber connectivity to West Coast interconnection points, factors that have positioned the Phoenix metro as a secondary US AI infrastructure hub. Arizona's arid climate creates water-supply pressure on cooling-intensive facilities, a regional constraint affecting long-term scaling at this site that is not reflected in published campus specifications.
